name: Casa Muffoletto
overview: A narrow, tall corner town house in Gratteri, in the Madonie mountains above Cefalù. Four storeys around one staircase: a cellar-style lounge and dining room at street level, a bedroom with en suite on each of the next two floors, and at the top the kitchen, the lounge under the open roof and two terraces. This site is the record of every room — what's there, what it will become, and the jobs to get it there.

floors.name: Ground floor
floors.notes: Street level on Largo Pietra Rossa: the lounge and dining room, the entrance hall with the arched front door, and a low store under the stairs. Studio A3's 2026 drawing proposed a new sewer pipe under the lounge floor — the owners have confirmed it is not needed.

floors.name: First floor
floors.notes: Bedroom with French window to Largo Pietra Rossa, and a new en-suite shower room in the former side room — built as Studio A3 proposed (Apr 2026), finishing works under way.

floors.name: Second floor
floors.notes: Main bedroom, opening onto the wrought-iron front balcony, with a new en-suite shower room in the angled side wing.

floors.name: Top floor
floors.notes: Bathroom, fridge & utility room, kitchen, the lounge under the open roof with its attic ledge, and two terraces. Much changed since the 2024 survey: walls removed, new terrace doors, ceiling opened up.

style.direction: Each floor has its own mood, held together by the staircase and by the house's old materials — beams, stone, cement tiles, plasterwork, wrought iron. Rich, earthy, slightly theatrical colour rather than white minimalism; antiques and character pieces kept; black and brass for metal throughout.
principles: Keep and show the original features: beams, exposed stone and rock, patterned cement-tile floors, plaster cornices, the iron balustrade, old doors and built-in cupboards
One strong colour idea per floor: navy at street level, deep green on the first floor, mushroom with a terracotta ceiling on the second, warm white under the open roof at the top
The staircase ties it together: terracotta limewash above deep olive
Green is the house's thread — olive cupboards, teal kitchen, green bedroom, green front doors
Black fittings in every bathroom; brass for lights and handles
Breathable paints on old masonry — lime, mineral or silicate, not plastic emulsion

palette.name: Terracotta

materials: Exposed chestnut beams and boarded roof
Patterned cement tiles (first and second floors, landing)
Terracotta floor tiles (ground floor, back terrace)
Marble, terrazzo and stone stair treads
Glazed vertical tiles in blue, blue-grey and blush (bathrooms)
avoid: Plastic masonry paint on old or exterior walls
Mixed metal finishes in one room
